title: ui-flow app file
description: One ui-flow app: screens (an image each), hotspots on them and links between screens. Format version 1. See docs/file-format.md for the semantics that a schema cannot express (references between ids, coordinate systems, how loading treats errors).

format.description: Marks the file as a ui-flow app.

version.description: Format version. Files with a higher version than the program supports are rejected.

name.description: Name of the app, shown in the window title and the export.

startScreen.description: Id of the screen the flow (and the player) starts at. Empty or unknown: the first screen.

screens.description: Screens in drawing order (later ones are drawn on top on the canvas).

links.description: Interactions: arrows from a screen (or one of its hotspots) to a screen.

images.description: Embedded images, referenced by screens[].image. Written last so the structure stays at the top of the file.

id.description: Identifier. ui-flow generates "<kind>-<n>" (screen-3, hotspot-7, link-2, img-4) with one counter for the whole file, but any non-empty string unique among its kind works.
Unique among screens (duplicates make the file invalid).

image.description: Id of an entry in images[]. Unknown: a grey placeholder is shown.

x.description: Canvas position of the image's top-left corner (canvas units).

scale.description: Canvas units per image pixel: the screen is (width * scale) x (height * scale) on the canvas. Non-positive values are read as 1.

hotspot.description: A clickable area of a screen. The rectangle is in image pixels (origin top-left), independent of the screen's scale.

id.description: Unique within its screen (ui-flow makes them unique in the whole file).

hotspot.description: Id of a hotspot of the source screen: clicking it follows the link. Absent (or empty): a described, screen-level transition.

to.description: Id of the target screen (may equal `from`).

message.description: What the user does, e.g. "user types command help". For hotspot links an optional note (condition, input...).

mime.description: Media type of `data`, e.g. image/png or image/jpeg (informative; the content is sniffed).

width.description: Pixel size of the decoded image. Used for layout without decoding: must match the data.

data.description: The original image file (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, TGA, PSD...) in standard base64, unchanged. Line breaks are tolerated when reading.
